newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan bourse ends down on week, SGBCI in demand.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan bourse ends down on week, SGBCI in demand.

text.p: The Abidjan bourse ended lower on the week and trade was slow, but the first listing of food oils producer Trituraf and a surge in demand for bank SGBCI provided talking points.
The BVA all-shares index fell 2.08 percent on the week to 496.59, but was still almost 39 percent up on the year so far, according to bourse data.

The value of shares and bonds traded during the week fell to 264.5 million CFA francs from 388 million the week before, and 42 percent of the total was in SGBCI shares, which rose 600 CFA francs to 30,000. The buyer, or buyers, were not revealed.
Publisher CEDA was also in demand, adding 600 to 13,600.
Against that, cement producer SOCIMAT fell 2,100 to 42,000.

Trituraf, majority-owned by Unilever, entered the bourse after the privatisation of the government's 10 percent stake. The issue sold out in four days and was oversubscribed by 107.5 percent, the bourse said.
The shares were introduced at the offer price of 6,250 CFA francs. They will begin trading at the next session on Tuesday, August 5.
